scope: Model/editor rewrite review for Lessons 0014–0020 after activity-variety, load, naturalness and skill-mix revisions; not an independent human review.

englishNaturalness.evidence: Do you have a pen? and Yes. Here you go. are natural classroom exchanges between classmates.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Checked learner-facing Persian for meaning, clarity and current Nova orthography rules; wording stays colloquial and context-specific.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: Familiar nouns are reused so the only main new language burden is have and the possession-question frame.

distractorQuality.evidence: Listening distractors use familiar object categories and avoid surface-form giveaways.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: A classmate checking for a pen before an exercise is plausible and useful.

difficultyFit.evidence: The Lesson introduces one construction and reuses established classroom vocabulary.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: The question is heard for meaning, reconstructed in writing-like assembly, then retrieved with a changed object.

transferQuality.evidence: book and pen move from request language into possession questions.

overallCoherence.evidence: All activities center on asking whether someone has a familiar object.

learnerExperience.evidence: Static flow review only. Activity order is more varied and help/feedback paths are present, but no real learner, microphone, timing or retention test has been performed.

limitations: Real learner outcomes and delayed retention have not been measured.
Generated audio still requires perceptual/prosody review with human listeners.
Hidden-answer retrieval remains bounded and cannot certify open-ended language ability.
resolvedFindings: The Lesson introduces one construction and reuses established classroom vocabulary.
book and pen move from request language into possession questions.
All activities center on asking whether someone has a familiar object.
